title: Quake bootable
wikitext:
{{Infobox | name = Ciscon's Quake Bootable | logo = | screenshot = | caption = Bootable Linux image for instant QuakeWorld play | developer = Ciscon | released = 2017 | operating_system = Linux (Debian-based live image) | platform = x86 PC | genre = Live operating system / game client image | license = Community distribution | website = }} '''Ciscon's Quake Bootable''' is a community-created bootable Linux image designed specifically for playing '''[[QuakeWorld]]''' online. Created by the QuakeWorld community member [[Ciscon]], the image is a lightweight Debian-based system which includes the [[ezQuake]] client, allowing users to quickly join online QuakeWorld servers without installing a full operating system. The image was primarily intended for use from a USB flash drive and became known within the QuakeWorld community as an easy way to turn almost any compatible PC into a dedicated Quake machine. '''[https://github.com/ciscon/quake-bootable Download]''' == Overview == The system is based on a minimal '''Debian Linux''' installation configured to run QuakeWorld flawlessly. It also includes some apps, for example [[Discord]]. Its purpose is to provide: * Fast boot directly into QuakeWorld * Minimal system overhead * Compatibility with NVIDIA, Intel, and AMD graphics hardware * Portable USB-based gameplay setup (but can also be installed to a hard drive) * Easy troubleshooting via terminal access == Installation == See the full [https://github.com/ciscon/quake-bootable instructions in Github]. == Features == === USB portability === The image is distributed as a compressed disk image file that can be written directly to a USB flash drive (or HDD!) using tools such as: * dd on Linux * Win32 Disk Imager, Rufus on Windows === Driver handling === The image includes support for NVIDIA hardware and attempts to remove NVIDIA-specific packages automatically when booted on non-NVIDIA systems. == Reception == Within the QuakeWorld community, the image was regarded as a convenient solution for quickly setting up Linux-based Quake clients. It was often compared to packages such as [[nQuake]], though its main advantage was being completely bootable without requiring installation on the host machine. == Troubleshooting == tbd == See also == * [[NQuake]] * [[Smooth Quake in Linux]] * [[Benchmark]] == FAQ == ==== Does it require installation? ==== No. It is intended to run as a live boot system from a USB drive OR hard disk drive. It requires the full disk to be used, as it is a system image. So if you want to keep your Windows, you need to have a 2nd hard drive to install Quake Bootable. If you don't have, keep reading. ==== My PC only has one physical disk - how to install? ==== You can boot from a Live Linux USB, then [https://github.com/ciscon/quake-bootable get the img] and burn it to the physical disk. You can use Quake bootable for this ;) using dd. ==== Can I use the same physical disk with another operating system? ==== Once Quake Bootable is installed, is a normal Linux. You can resize the partition and install Windows or other Operating System if you want.
If the partition is set as LVM, you'll need to resize the filesystem before you resize the partition. sudo lvresize --resizefs --size 100GB /dev/YOURMOUNTPOINT/ROOT_FS Replace 100GB with the size you need for your quakebootable OS (20GB should give you some headroom). The remaining space will be unallocated, ready to be used by other OS. ==== Is it still maintained? ==== As of 2026 - yes! '''[https://github.com/ciscon/quake-bootable Download]''' ==== Can I use it offline? ==== Yes, but its main purpose is online '''QuakeWorld''' multiplayer. ==== Timezone is inconsistent! ==== To fix, need to run a command. First identify your timezone with sudo timedatectl list-timezones. Then set the timezone with sudo timedatectl set-timezone . ==== I have more questions! ==== Visit [https://github.com/ciscon/quake-bootable Github page]. If it doesn't help, you can ask [[Ciscon]] on Discord. [[Category:Packages]]
